e-9704.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of an Object
e-9704.problem: At full speed, a fully grown cheetah can cover a distance of $998$ feet in $10$ seconds. What is the speed of the cheetah when running at full speed?
e-9704.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed in feet per second, we divide the number of feet, $998,$ by the number of seconds, $10.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{998}{10} & =99.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the cheetah is $99.8$ feet per second.

e-9705.knowledge_point: Calculating Distance Given Speed and Time
e-9705.problem: Moving at a constant rate, it takes $8$ seconds for a particular type of fish to swim a distance of $200$ centimeters. Find the distance this fish can cover in $3$ seconds.
e-9705.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in centimeters per second, we divide the number of centimeters, $200,$ by the number of seconds, $8.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{200}{8} & =200÷8 \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the fish is $25$ centimeters per second. 

To find the distance covered in $3$ seconds, we multiply the speed by $3.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{distance} & =\text{speed}\times \text{time} \\  & =25\times 3 \\  & =75.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fish can cover $75$ centimeters in $3$ seconds.

e-9706.knowledge_point: Calculating Time Given Distance and Speed
e-9706.problem: It takes $5$ days for the Earth to travel $13$ million kilometers around the Sun. How much time does it take for the Earth to travel $52$ million kilometers around the Sun?
e-9706.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in millions of kilometers per day, we divide the number of million kilometers, $13,$ by the number of days, $5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{5} & =13÷5 \\  & =2.6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the Earth is $2.6$ million kilometers per day. 

To find the time it takes the Earth to cover $52$ million kilometers, we divide the distance by $2.6.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{52}{2.6} \\  & =\frac{52\times 10}{2.6\times 10} \\  & =\frac{520}{26} \\  & =520÷26 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it takes the Earth $20$ days to travel $52$ million kilometers around the Sun.

A bike traveled 240 kilometers at a constant speed of 40 kilometers per hour. For how long was the bike in motion?

a
8 hours
b
40 hours
c
7 hours
d
6 hours
e
12 hours
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The speed is 40 kilometers per hour. To find the time it took the bike to cover 240 kilometers, we divide the distance by 40. This gives

time=distancespeed=24040=240÷1040÷10=244=6.

Therefore, the bike was in motion for 6 hours.

content.problem: A bike traveled $240$ kilometers at a constant speed of $40$ kilometers per hour. For how long was the bike in motion?
content.worked_solution:
The speed is $40$ kilometers per hour. To find the time it took the bike to cover $240$ kilometers, we divide the distance by $40.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{240}{40} \\  & =\frac{240÷10}{40÷10} \\  & =\frac{24}{4} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the bike was in motion for $6$ hours.
